name: RTX CORPORATION
naics_description: RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT IN THE PHYSICAL, ENGINEERING, AND LIFE SCIENCES (EXCEPT NANOTECHNOLOGY AND BIOTECHNOLOGY)
brief_text:
Three detectors fired for RTX Corporation. Benford's Law analysis found significant deviation in the leading-digit distribution of award amounts, with observed frequencies departing notably from expected natural patterns across all nine digits. Modification growth on contract SPE4AX20DR001 expanded at a rate far exceeding peers in the same industry code, suggesting unusually aggressive contract value escalation. Isolation Forest flagged the entity as a multivariate outlier based on its combined profile of total dollars, award volume, agency concentration, and modification patterns.

The Benford test yielded a KS statistic of 0.094 with p-value 4.1e-15 across 1,904 transactions. The worst-performing contract showed a modification growth ratio of 7,504.6 compared to a NAICS average of 30.2, producing a z-score of 20.18. The Isolation Forest anomaly score was 0.934 on a scale where higher values indicate greater statistical deviation from typical peer behavior.

These signals reflect statistical anomalies rather than proof of misconduct. RTX is a major defense contractor with $47 billion in lifetime obligations and 1,904 awards, primarily from a single agency. The scale and concentration of activity, combined with the nature of large-scale defense R&D contracting involving frequent modifications, may naturally produce patterns that diverge from smaller-peer baselines. The Benford deviation warrants review but does not inherently indicate fraud in high-volume contract environments.
